summary.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose over 115% YoY to INR37 crores at a 5.3% margin; FY26 EBITDA up 25% to INR85 crores on 3% lower income.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the best quarter of the year, with standalone total income of INR699 crores (up 4% YoY) and gross margin of 45% (up 329 bps YoY). For FY26, standalone income fell 3% to INR2,585 crores while EBITDA rose 25% to INR85 crores at a 3.3% margin, and management said the year was cash positive. Home textiles turned EBITDA-positive at INR8.4 crores (from negative INR3.5 crores), and the company is guiding FY27 as a year of margin expansion, profitability and deleveraging, without giving numeric targets. Management also flagged losses at the US subsidiary American Silk Mills, which is being closed or muted; India operations reported no inventory losses.

financial_highlights.change: from negative INR3.5 crores in FY25

financial_highlights.value: 0.8% in Q1 to 5.3% in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation at 93%, with effective spindle utilisation at about 89%. Management is prioritising value-added yarns over volume; cotton melange ranks highest on profitability, followed by PV dyed and 100% cotton.

segments.name: Fiber (Sutlej Green Fiber)
segments.commentary: Recycled polyester and sustainable fiber business operating at over 100% utilisation in FY26, described as a breakout year and a strategic ESG-aligned platform.

segments.name: Home textiles
segments.commentary: Turned EBITDA-positive at INR8.4 crores in FY26 versus negative INR3.5 crores. Order pipeline is at 180 days. Management says it expects at least a doubling of EBITDA next year. Nesterra brand is run on a working-capital-light model through LFS and MBO partners, with no franchise or own stores yet.

segments.name: US subsidiary (American Silk Mills)
segments.commentary: Inventory losses sit in this US holding, not India operations. Management has decided to close or mute the unit and will serve US home textile customers directly, with US about 60% of exports.

guidance_outlook: FY27 is expected to be the inflection year: EBITDA to expand meaningfully on the FY26 base, profitability to return after almost two years of losses, and debt metrics to improve as cash generation strengthens. No numeric targets given.
Target to convert about one-third of the yarn portfolio into value-added segments over the next 12 months.
Renewable energy share to rise from 11% to about 40%, aimed at reducing power cost, which is about 50% of yarn manufacturing cost.
Home textiles EBITDA expected to at least double in the coming year, per management, though no number was put on it.
Technical textiles entry, beginning with protective textiles, will be capital-efficient and use existing assets plus incremental capex; protective textile margins cited at 12-15%.
Capex for FY27 is higher than FY26 (about INR70 crores spent in FY26) and milestone-based; more definite numbers expected in one to two quarters.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was roughly INR70 crores; FY27 budget is higher and released quarter by quarter against milestones.
Yarn capacity utilisation 93%; effective spindle utilisation about 89%.
Sutlej Green Fiber running at over 100% utilisation and being revamped further.
Home textile processing capacity of about 2 million meters; technical textiles will add specific equipment on top of this.
demand_pricing: Yarn prices have risen in line with raw material costs (polyester up about 30%, with viscose, acrylic and cotton also rising). Management says there is no incremental margin gain, only margin protection.
Global apparel demand is soft as customers run inventories tight. The US destocked over the last 3-4 quarters, and tariff clarity may be starting to bring in inquiries.
Export mix: about 60% of total business is exports, and about 60% of that goes to the US.
Value-added product feedback loop (sampling to test orders) takes 6-9 months.
Inventory policy: about 30-45 days of cotton and 15-20 days of other fibres.

qa_highlights.question: How much will yarn price increases since March lift the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Srivastava said yarn price increases only match raw material cost increases (polyester up about 30%), so there is no incremental contribution, only margin protection.

qa_highlights.question: Why are there inventory losses when prices are rising, and will more be booked this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No inventory losses in India. The losses are in the US subsidiary American Silk Mills, which is being closed or muted; US exports will now be served directly.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Nesterra revenue stagnated for 4-6 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: The brand follows a calibrated, working-capital-efficient plan with LFS and MBO partners, with no own stores or franchise yet, so growth is deliberately measured.

qa_highlights.question: Will the yarn margin return to 10%+ EBITDA, and what is the blended yarn mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers. It cited higher power costs and older cotton machinery as the cause of the dip, with renewables and value-added mix as the fix, and said YoY EBITDA margin improvement is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What margins are expected from technical textiles, and which sectors are targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Protective textile margins of 12-15%, depending on inherent or treated FR. Target sectors include oil and gas and steel, with the application base much wider.

qa_highlights.question: Home textile EBITDA trajectory and whether INR18-20 crores in two years is realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it is confident of at least doubling home textile EBITDA next year on the order book and strategic customer commitments.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (polyester, viscose, cotton) and whether yarn price pass-through holds.
Forex hedging discipline, global tariff uncertainty and borrowing cost, named as watch areas.
Losses and closure costs at the US subsidiary American Silk Mills.
Value-added yarn and technical textiles depend on 6-9 month qualification cycles and product consistency.
Capex pace is milestone-linked, and FY27 capex figures are not yet defined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the margin-led turnaround and FY27 direction, but evasive on quantified targets for yarn margins, home textile EBITDA and capex. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers and cited milestone-based planning.
key_quotes: That combination, margin expansion through a softer top line year in an environment we have just described is the most important number on this call.
The division swung from a negative INR3.5 crores to a positive INR8.4 crores at the EBITDA level in the last financial year.
We are not chasing growth for the sake of growth.
So what I can tell you is; last year, as per our numbers, we have done roughly about INR70 crores, which has kind of gone in.

adds.what: Home textile processing capacity of about 2 million meters (existing; technical textiles to add specific equipment on top, no size given)
Sutlej Green Fiber revamp (running over 100% utilisation, further revamp; no size given)
Technical textiles / protective textiles entry using existing assets plus incremental capex (no size or timeline given)

growth.why: FY27 guided as an inflection year with EBITDA to expand meaningfully on FY26 (INR85 cr) and home textile EBITDA to at least double, but no numeric revenue target; backing is partial (renewable power share rise to ~40%, one-third of yarn portfolio to value-added in 12 months, 180-day home textile order pipeline, 93% yarn utilisation) with no specific new capacity commissioning numbers or timelines.
